report.rationale: E16 selects branch B, and E07 establishes normal polarity. Circulation loss is the only candidate compatible with all three physical measurements. Each competing candidate is contradicted by at least one measurement. E03 identifies the cached estimator as stale. The shared reliability regime warrants residual uncertainty; these probabilities are judgmental, not an exact posterior. The strongest alternative is tied with sensor bias and actuator stiction.

E16 selects branch B, and E07 confirms normal polarity. Circulation loss is the unique intersection of the compatibility sets in E11, E13, and E14. Sensor bias, actuator stiction, and none of the above each conflict with one measurement; controller timing fault conflicts with all three. E03 establishes estimator staleness, not a particular fault. No stronger alternative is supported; none of the above is a representative of the three tied single-conflict alternatives. Shared reliability prevents treating the measurements as independent confirmations. The probabilities are judgmental allocations, not calibrated posteriors, because priors and error rates are unspecified.

Estimator freshness and the shared reliability regime remain unverified; no physical measurements were acquired. These probabilities are provisional rather than an exactly calibrated posterior.
